T0468.title: Social Engineering
T0468.definition: The practice of manipulating individuals through psychological tactics to divulge confidential information, grant unauthorized access, or perform actions that compromise security, bypassing technical controls by exploiting human psychology.
T0468.description: Social engineering targets human judgment rather than directly defeating a technical control. Attackers exploit trust, authority, urgency, fear, or greed through impersonation, pretexts, and pressure to obtain credentials, verification codes, sensitive information, transfers, software installation, or access. Common techniques include phishing, executive or support impersonation, phone pretexts, fabricated emergencies, invented identities, and physical tailgating. Modern operations combine open-source intelligence, breached data, AI voice cloning, and deepfakes to appear more credible; phishing, account takeover, and transfer fraud are specific outcomes of this shared manipulation method.
T0468.usageExample: An attacker called an employee impersonating IT support, created urgency by claiming a security incident required immediate password reset, and successfully obtained credentials that provided access to corporate systems.
